items.title: Kraft Heinz isn't afraid to get cheesy with its NFL sponsorship
items.summary: Halfway through year one of a five-year global NFL partnership covering Kraft, Velveeta, Philadelphia and Kraft Mac & Cheese, Kraft Heinz is weaving its brands into fan moments in playful ways. Its Thanksgiving weekend activation, Velveeta Pylon Plays, makes US fans eligible to win Velveeta via Uber Eats when a touchdown scorer hits an end-zone pylon, with no branding on the pylons themselves. Heinz also sponsors Prime Video's Red Zone Moments, and the company says Heinz dollar sales rose 20% in the week of its NFL Draft activation compared with the same week in 2025.
items.what_it_means: A portfolio sponsor is tying its brands to in-game moments fans already watch for, and reporting a sales lift from it.

items.title: Dynamo see 20% revenue surge as attendance, partnerships grow
items.summary: Houston Dynamo revenue rose 20% between the 2025 and 2026 seasons, according to President of Business Operations Jessica O'Neill, citing the Houston Business Journal. Dynamo home attendance grew 6% to 18,719 a match and the NWSL's Houston Dash grew 14%, while new national partners included LaCroix, Kroger, Dude Wipes and Higginbotham. O'Neill credits growth in lead generation: the club aimed to double new leads across both teams in 2026 and is on pace to triple them, which fed attendance, digital engagement and community event turnout.
items.what_it_means: A mid-market club tied its revenue growth to building a much larger pipeline of new fan leads.

items.title: Sports Media Pod: Amazon is bringing new advertisers to the NFL
items.summary: On SBJ's Sports Media Podcast, Amazon Ads executive Billy Davis tells Josh Carpenter that Prime Video has attracted 80 brands that had never advertised in the NFL before. He also discusses Amazon bringing new advertisers to the NBA and to its wider sports portfolio.
items.what_it_means: Streaming rights holders are widening the pool of brands buying into live sport, beyond the traditional NFL advertisers.

items.title: NBA Europe formalizes $10.9B fund to infuse future arenas
items.summary: The NBA has created a $10.9B initiative, backed by firms including Apollo Sports Capital, Ares, Arctos, Blackstone, HPS, J.P. Morgan, Sixth Street and Stonepeak, to help future NBA Europe franchises build or renovate arenas and develop mixed-use districts around them. The league has pointed prospective owners to a 2024 Accenture study projecting San Francisco's Chase Center and Thrive City contributed $4.2B to the local economy over five years. Deputy Commissioner Mark Tatum called it a 5 to 20 year project that is about enhancing the fan experience, with initial franchises expected to be formalised as soon as Q1 2027.
items.what_it_means: The NBA is treating venues and the districts around them as the core of its European business case.

items.title: Column: College football tailgating is going corporate
items.summary: Summarising Will Leitch in The Athletic, SBJ reports that athletic departments taking control of tailgating spots has become a nationwide trend. RevelXP, founded by a private equity firm to reimagine gameday and non-gameday experiences, now has deals with more than two-thirds of Power 4 schools, and The Grove at Ole Miss is now more than three-quarters vendor based. Leitch argues there is a long-term cost in turning a tradition passed between generations into another revenue line.
items.what_it_means: Monetising fan traditions around the game brings new revenue and a risk of eroding what made them valuable.

items.title: Price cuts drive Corona Capital's 'best year in three years'
items.summary: OCESA's Corona Capital in Mexico City sold 220,000 tickets for its 20-22 November festival, its strongest sales in three years, after cutting ticket prices by 10% and making its first concerted push to sell to American fans. OCESA's Memo Parra says the cut was driven by the volume of stadium and arena shows passing through Mexico, framing fans' choice as going to Bruno Mars or the festival. Savings came from many small budget cuts, including catering and crew scheduling, while attendance was roughly level with 2019.
items.what_it_means: Festivals compete with every other big night out for the same fan budget, and some are cutting costs to win it.

items.title: Fanatics sees record year of retail sales for NFL International Games
items.summary: Fanatics says merchandise sales across its NFL Shop city-centre and stadium stores for the International Games season rose more than 40% on 2025, across eight games in six countries including first regular-season games in Melbourne, Rio de Janeiro and Paris. More than 250,000 fans visited NFL stores, and Munich set the record for single game-day sales at a European NFL game. Online NFL merchandise sales through Fanatics' channels rose 17% across London's three game weeks.
items.what_it_means: International games are working as retail events that reach fans well beyond the stadium.

items.title: U.S. Ski & Snowboard carrying commercial momentum into domestic FIS events
items.summary: U.S. Ski & Snowboard is hosting a record 14 FIS World Cups this season, more than double four years ago, with more than 20 sponsors including a new Dick's Sporting Goods deal. CEO Sophie Goldschmidt says home events give brands more chances to activate and meet fans, and that the brand is becoming more aspirational and lifestyle-led to reach casual fans. NBC will air every alpine World Cup race, and USSS and FIS are launching a YouTube and FAST channel, alongside a second Togethxr merch collaboration, 'Everyone Watches Women's Skiing'.
items.what_it_means: A national governing body is growing sponsorship by hosting more home events and courting casual fans.

items.title: NWSL Championship is league's second-best audience yet, but down 6% from 2025
items.summary: CBS averaged 1.12 million viewers for the KC Current's NWSL championship win over the Washington Spirit, down 6% on last year's record 1.18 million but the league's second-best audience. Women 21 and older made up 47% of the audience, its largest ever in that demo, up from 42%. The postseason averaged 610,000 viewers over six telecasts, up 11% on 2025, after regular-season viewership fell 19% ahead of the final year of current rights deals in 2027.
items.what_it_means: The NWSL's big moments are holding audience while regular-season viewing softens ahead of a rights renewal.

items.title: Essence Festival Officially Leaving New Orleans
items.summary: The Essence Festival of Music and Culture, one of the largest Black festivals in the US, is leaving New Orleans after more than three decades, officials confirmed to Pollstar. Negotiations between the city and festival leaders stalled over contracts and vendor payments, and the city's contract expired in September. Organiser Sundial Media Group said the festival generated more than $300 million in economic impact for New Orleans and Louisiana in 2025.
items.what_it_means: Major festivals are portable assets, and host cities can lose them when the partnership terms break down.
